subject: Proposal: incremental commit bridge + staggered onboarding playbook
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jenny Park <jenny.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: incremental commit bridge + staggered onboarding playbook

Hi Jenny —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, attached is a short proposal that sketches an incremental-commit path (24-month umbrella with staged ramp windows) plus a staggered onboarding playbook so your engineering teams can scale capacity without a one-time heavy commit. High level:

- Year 1: smaller committed base (30% of expected peak) with two 6-month ramp windows.
- Year 2: automatic annualization of remaining committed capacity with optional quarterly true-ups.
- Fallbacks: automatic model-tier fallback and burst credits for the first 90 days of onboarding.

This structure keeps your initial spend predictable while preserving headroom for spikes during migration. I also called out a co-term option if you want to align to a March fiscal boundary (we can pro-rate the trailing months).

Attachments: ACME_incremental_commit_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal)

Can you review and let me know the procurement constraints (quarterly vs annual invoicing, PO timing) and whether a 24-month umbrella works for your CFO? If helpful, we can convert to a vendor-friendly 12+12 with defined true-up triggers.

Cheers,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Account Strategy | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
T: +1 415-555-0126

From: Jenny Park <jenny.park@acmecloud.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: incremental commit bridge + staggered onboarding playbook

Evelyn —

Thanks for the detailed proposal. High level this looks promising. A few notes/questions from our side:

- Procurement prefers co-terming to our fiscal year (Mar 31) — we need clarity on proration and effective date if we do a 24-month umbrella that starts mid-fiscal.
- Can we do quarterly true-ups instead of annual true-ups for the early ramp so we can adjust spend more frequently?
- Our security/compliance team asked about data residency for the first 90-day burst periods (are those routed to our EU-only pool if we opt for that?).

I looped in procurement so they can weigh in on invoicing cadence and PO timing. If you can provide a version that maps to our March co-term and shows a quarterly true-up example, procurement will be able to give a rapid approval.

Also, can you include a sample onboarding schedule that shows how we move 3 teams across the ramp windows (we want to avoid a single-day cutover).

Thanks — Jenny
Jenny Park
Head of Platform Partnerships, Acme Cloud
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jenny Park <jenny.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: incremental commit bridge + staggered onboarding playbook

Jenny / procurement team —

Great questions. Summarizing and proposing adjustments inline: 

1) Co-term and proration
- We can co-term to your Mar 31 fiscal boundary. If the 24-month umbrella starts on Jun 1, we pro-rate the first partial fiscal year (Jun 1 – Mar 31) and then align subsequent renewals to Mar 31. Example numbers included in the attached spreadsheet.

2) Quarterly true-ups
- We can make the early ramp true-ups quarterly for Year 1 (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4 style) and then switch to semi-annual in Year 2 if you prefer. Trigger = 120% of committed baseline for the preceding quarter.

3) Data residency during burst
- Burst requests honor routing policy. If you select EU-only for certain environments, bursts will be routed to your designated pool by region. We'll document SLOs for cross-region fallback in the SLR section.

4) Staggered onboarding schedule
- Attached: onboarding-staggered-plan.xlsx — sample 12-week rollout for 3 teams, with week-by-week checkpoints, training, and throttled ramp percentages so capacity increases happen over 8–10 weeks per team.

Next steps:
- If procurement confirms quarterly invoicing is OK, we will: 1) finalize financials and discounts for the 24-month umbrella, 2) issue a non-binding term sheet for internal legal review, and 3) generate a signature-ready DocuSign.

Karthik and Marissa have visibility on pricing and SLRs — I've asked them to confirm discount tiers and the co-term proration math in a follow-up note.

Best,
Evelyn

Attachments: onboarding-staggered-plan.xlsx
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Proposal: incremental commit bridge + staggered onboarding playbook

Hi Jenny —

Following up from finance/ops: we can support quarterly invoicing for Year 1, and we are prepared to offer a 7.5% contract discount if Acme signs a 24-month umbrella and agrees to early payment terms (net 30). I've updated the HubSpot deal (link below) with the pricing table and proration examples.

DocuSign: if procurement is ready, I pushed a draft Term Sheet to DocuSign to accelerate execution: https://www.docusign.com/sign?tr=abc123-placeholder

Key callouts for procurement:
- Invoice cadence: Quarterly in Year 1 (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct style after proration alignment).
- True-up triggers: Quarterly in Y1, switch to semi-annual in Y2 unless otherwise requested.
- Early payment: 7.5% discount applied to committed spend if net-30 is accepted.

If procurement confirms acceptance of quarterly invoicing and net-30 early pay, we will route the DocuSign and set a 30-day execution target. Happy to hop on a short call to walk procurement through the proration table.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
